title: Travelers Lose Nearly $2,500 to Trip Troubles
paragraphs: Travel can be fun, but things do not always go as planned. According to a new survey, problems on trips can cost travelers a lot of money.

The survey was done by Talker Research for Aven Hospitality, a company that makes technology for hotels. It asked 4,000 people about their travel experiences. Half of them were from the United States, and the other half were from the UK and Australia.
The survey found that 73% of people had a big problem on a trip at some time. On average, they said these problems cost them almost $2,500.

What were the most common problems? Bad weather was the biggest problem, at 26%. Next was getting sick or hurt, at 16%. Other common problems were arriving at a hotel and finding that something it promised was not available, having a phone with no battery or internet at an important time and getting lost. Each of these happened to 14% of people.
One person said, "I broke my leg on the second day of a 14-day trip."

About half of the travelers, 51%, said that their problems happened because they did not have correct information when they planned their trips. Because of this, 85% said they changed the way they plan and book trips.
Many travelers now use AI to help them. In the survey, 67% said they had used AI tools to search for travel information.
Younger travelers lost more money than older travelers. Millennials said they lost $2,496 on average, but baby boomers said they lost $956.
